program: Master in Immersive Audio (Focus Master)
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited — part of the accredited Master of Music (Master Muziek) of Amsterdamse Hogeschool voor de Kunsten (AHK). AHK is a government-funded (bekostigd) HBO institution and therefore an IND recognised sponsor for study residence permits.

Year 1 foundation modules in immersive production across classical, jazz, pop and electronic genres, plus acoustics, mixing, production and management. Year 2 specialisation in either composing OR production for immersive audio, with research and capstone project. institution: Conservatorium Maastricht — Zuyd University of Applied Sciences (Zuyd Hogeschool)
program: Master of Music — Electronic Music Performance (EMP), Jazz department
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited Master of Music (Zuyd Hogeschool, CROHO). Zuyd is a government-funded HBO institution and therefore an IND recognised sponsor for study residence permits (the site itself notes 'Non European applicants will receive a questionnaire around May ... for the application of the resident Visa/residence permit').
language: English — 'The programmes of Master of Music are taught in English.'
durationEcts: 2 years full-time. Curriculum table shows 60 ECTS in Year 1 and 60 in Year 2 (Main Subject 29/24, Band & Performing 6/6, Recording & Producing 2/2, Composing & Arranging 2/2, Tools in Creation 4/4, Current Jazz 2/2, Impro Lab 2/2, Master Research 5/10, Health & Well-being 1/1, Your Art as a Business 3/3, Outreach 2/2, Elective Modules 6/6) = 120 ECTS.
whatYouStudy: 'Currently, electronic musicians everywhere are searching for ways to include more live elements in their performance and Jazz musicians are exploring the possibilities of electronic music. The EMP (Electronic Music Performance) programme prepares you for a successful career at the junction of those two directions. The idea is to get the sound directly from your head into songs and, more importantly: on stage. Produce music at a professional level and then perform it, in new creative ways, with talented musicians. Making the most of all the possibilities music technology has to offer.' Modules include Introduction to Studio Recording & Music Production, Band & Performing, Composing & Arranging, Tools in Creation, Current Jazz, Impro Lab, Master Research, Your Art as a Business.
entryRequirements: 'To study a Master programme at Conservatorium Maastricht, you must hold one of the following: A Bachelor's degree in Music, or proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme.'
acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONAL — the quoted rule allows 'proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme' in place of a Bachelor of Music. In practice that equivalence is demonstrated through the portfolio and live audition, which demand instrumental playing and jazz skills. Note also that Conservatorium Maastricht runs a Preparatory Course Master: 'you will be notified whether you have been admitted to: the Master programme, the Preparatory Course Master, or if your application has been rejected' — a genuine one-year bridging route for a candidate who is close but not yet at master level. This is one of the more realistic Dutch options for a non-music graduate, but the jazz/instrumental demands are real.
portfolioSpec: Video portfolio, un-edited recordings, uploaded to YouTube as 'unlisted', LINKS ONLY (do not send files). Content required: (1) candidate presents him/herself in English at the start of the video, maximum 10 minutes long; (2) THREE own productions in a DAW (originals) — 'Show the entire production and then talk us through which tools and techniques you've used in those productions'; (3) 'A video of you playing on your instrument' — one video per instrument if multiple; 'It's important to show your jazz skills where you have them. Playing (jazz) piano and/or guitar is a plus!' Optional additional content: a live-performance video, and scores/leadsheets via a public cloud-folder link (PDF).
auditionSpec: YES — online live audition plus a separate interview. 'Depending on your level, you will be invited for an online meeting with the teachers for an online "live" audition. During the "live" audition, we will discuss your portfolio and you present us your vision. You should be ready to show your playing skills on your preferred instrument and piano ... The main subject teachers also may take time to test your ears ... The most important focus, however, will be on the quality of your writing and your vision! The "live" audition should take 20 – 45 minutes.' Then: 'you will be invited for an interview with the jazz master coordinator to discuss your study and research plans. The master interview should take approximately 20 minutes.' Audition dates: first-round 15 March – 15 April; second-round 15 May – 15 June.

acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY. portfolioSpec: 'All suitable candidates will be required to submit a portfolio prior to acceptance on the course.
